Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative due to the limited precision of floating-point representations, which can lead to rounding errors. When the order of operations changes, the intermediate results may differ, causing the final result to vary. This discrepancy arises because small differences in the least significant bits can be lost when adding numbers of significantly different magnitudes.

Floating-point addition is not associative due to the limited precision of floating-point representations, which can lead to rounding errors. When adding three numbers, the order of operations can affect the intermediate results, causing different rounding errors depending on how the numbers are grouped. As a result, \( (a + b) + c \) may yield a different result than \( a + (b + c) \), demonstrating the non-associative nature of floating-point addition.
